newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic wins access to Angeion patents.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic wins access to Angeion patents.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said on Tuesday that a recent binding arbitration decision has given the company access to a specific group of defibrillator patents held by Angeion Corp.

In arbitration of a dispute between Medtronic and St. Jude Medical Inc, arbitrator William Webster held that a patent litigation settlement and license agreement between Medtronic and Siemens AG dated August 26, 1992 applied to patents licensed by Angeion to Siemens before the arrhythmia management business of Siemens was acquired by St. Jude.

The arbitrator ruled that Medtronic is the duly authorized sub-licensee on a non-exclusive worldwide basis of all of the "exclusive Angeion defibrillator patents" derived from applications filed before August 1, 1992.
The "exclusive Angeion defibrillator patents" are all of the defibrillator patents exclusively licensed by Angeion to Siemens-Pacesetter Inc on February 4, 1993.
Pacesetter is now a division of St. Jude.
Medtronic is a medical technology company specializing in implantable and invasive therapies.
